name: template-composition
body: Slide templates declare named sections, the section templates each accepts, and repeat limits (min/max, e.g. columns 2–4). A section template's `template.yaml` may declare `sections:` with exactly the schema slides use, so a section can hold sections of its own and composition nests. Nesting depth is bounded by the content syntax — heading depth is nesting depth — so no template composition chain may exceed six heading levels (`#`…`######`); this is checked at load, not configured (requirements.constraint.section-depth-limit). Reference cycles are rejected at load with the chain in the error (requirements.constraint.section-cycle-error-chain): a reference is a declared `sections:` acceptance, a `section` helper call in a layout, or a `child` constructor's template target (section-helper-load-checks, child-constructor), so two section templates whose layouts invoke each other through the helper are a cycle the same way a declared chain is. A `section` helper call may pass child sections as child arguments (`child` or `children`), each resolved like an authored instance against the target's declared `sections:`, so composition nests through helper calls as well as through headings. The depth bound counts heading-level composition; a helper call and its child arguments are references for cycle rejection but are not headings, so they do not by themselves extend the six-heading-level chain. A resolved child tree passed through a `section` helper is bounded at 64 nested child levels at render time: a deeper tree fails as a render error naming the bound (`section children nested too deeply: depth exceeds 64`) instead of recursing without bound, so a helper/child edge adds no heading depth, the six-heading-level bound is unchanged, and the render-time bound only rejects a runaway child tree. Sections accept only section templates (those under `templates/sections/`), never slide templates (those under `templates/slides/`; requirements.constraint.template-registry-integrity).
